papers.title_in_file: Quantum reservoir computing for photonic entanglement witnessing
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, discussion and part of the methods.
papers.what_it_is: An experiment that uses a quantum extreme learning machine on photon pairs to reconstruct entanglement witnesses.

assertions.value: The authors report that a quantum extreme learning machine (a memoryless form of quantum reservoir computing) reconstructed an entanglement witness for two-photon states with performance on par with methods that rely on careful calibration and prior knowledge of the apparatus.
quotes: We have experimentally demonstrated the capability of quantum reservoir computing, specifically in the QELM form, to reconstruct an entanglement witness for bipartite states of a two-photon system
achieving performance on par with methods that rely on careful calibration and prior knowledge of the apparatus
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result of one experimental study.

assertions.value: The authors state that training solely on separable states was sufficient to witness the entanglement of previously unseen input states, and that drifts in the experimental setup can leave the witness reconstruction largely unaffected.
quotes: training solely on separable states is sufficient to accurately witness the entanglement of new, previously unseen input states
drifts in the experimental setup can leave the final witness reconstruction largely unaffected
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result of one experimental study.

assertions.value: The authors state that they use the orbital angular momentum of photon pairs as an ancillary degree of freedom to enable informationally complete single-setting measurements of the photons' polarization.
quotes: We leverage the orbital angular momentum of photon pairs as an ancillary degree of freedom to enable informationally complete single-setting measurements of their polarization.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its experimental setup, Abstract, p.1.

papers.title_in_file: Variational Quantum Soft Actor-Critic for Robotic Arm Control
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of hybrid quantum-classical Soft Actor-Critic reinforcement learning on a virtual robotic arm.

assertions.value: The authors report that a boost in performance was observed when the Soft Actor-Critic used hybrid quantum-classical Critic networks, and that the quantum algorithm achieved the same performance as the classical algorithm with approximately six times fewer learnable parameters.
assertions.anchor: VII. Conclusions and Future Works, p.12
quotes: a boost in performance has been observed when the SAC algorithm leverages hybrid networks for the Critic components
the quantum algorithm achieves the same performance as the classical SAC with approximately six times fewer learnable parameters
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result of one simulation study.
assertions.reader_inference: The result is on digital simulation only and compares parameter counts, not runtime or hardware cost.

assertions.value: The authors report that no quantum advantage was found with a hybrid Actor component of the algorithm.
assertions.anchor: VII. Conclusions and Future Works, p.12
quotes: While no quantum advantage has been found with a hybrid Actor component of the algorithm
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical null result of one simulation study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the performance of the Variational Quantum Soft Actor-Critic on a virtual robotic arm was investigated by means of digital simulations of quantum circuits.
quotes: the performance of a Variational Quantum Soft Actor-Critic on the movement of a virtual robotic arm has been investigated by means of digital simulations of quantum circuits
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its scope: simulation, not hardware, Abstract, p.1.

papers.title_in_file: Scalable Parameter Design for Superconducting Quantum Circuits with Graph Neural Networks
papers.version_note: arXiv v3, 24 Jul 2025; the file name carries the earlier 2024 title and year.
papers.what_it_is: A graph neural network method for choosing gate frequencies in large superconducting quantum chips to reduce crosstalk error.

assertions.value: The authors report that for superconducting quantum circuits of around 870 qubits, their GNN-based algorithm achieves 51% of the errors produced by the state-of-the-art algorithm, with a time reduction from 90 min to 27 sec.
quotes: for large-scale superconducting quantum circuits consisting of around 870 qubits, our GNNs-based algorithm achieves 51% of the errors produced by the state-of-the-art algorithm, with a time reduction from 90 min to 27 sec.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result of one study on a simulated error model.

assertions.value: The authors state that the algorithm uses a three-stair scaling mechanism: an evaluator trained in a supervised way on small-scale circuits and applied to medium-scale circuits, and a designer trained in an unsupervised way on medium-scale circuits and applied to large-scale ones, demonstrated on quantum crosstalk errors.
quotes: an evaluator supervisedly trained on small-scale circuits for applying to medium-scale circuits
a designer unsupervisedly trained on medium-scale circuits for applying to large-scale ones
We demonstrate our algorithm in mitigating quantum crosstalk errors.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own description of its method and setup, Abstract, p.1.

assertions.value: The authors state that in future research additional error sources and variations between qubits may be taken into account, and that the evaluator may be trained using experimental data.
quotes: In the future research, additional error sources and variations between qubits may be taken into account, and the evaluator may be trained using experimental data
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own statement of what the current work leaves out, Discussion.
assertions.reader_inference: The evaluator in this work was not trained on experimental data.

papers.title_in_file: Evaluating the Impact of Different Quantum Kernels on the Classification Performance of Support Vector Machine Algorithm: A Medical Dataset Application
papers.what_it_is: A comparison of nine quantum feature maps in a quantum kernel SVM on two public medical datasets.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum kernel matrices from 9 different quantum feature maps were used in the QSVM-Kernel algorithm, and that the PCA value was set to 5 because of the limitations of NISQ computers.
quotes: quantum kernel matrices obtained from 9 different quantum feature maps were used
the PCA value was set to 5
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its experimental setup, Abstract and Conclusion.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the Wisconsin Breast Cancer (original) dataset two feature maps reached equal classification performance, and that the total execution time is about 2 times higher for the parametrized quantum circuit.
quotes: the QSVM Kernel algorithm achieves equal classification performance when
since the total execution time is about 2 times higher for the parametrized quantum circuit
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on one dataset; the gate symbols are lost in the text extraction.

assertions.value: The authors state that on the TCGA Glioma dataset one rotational-gate feature map gives better results in total processing time, but its classification performance value is too low to be generalized.
quotes: the classification performance value is too low to be generalized when it is used as a feature map
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's reading of an empirical result from one dataset.

papers.title_in_file: Contextuality and inductive bias in quantum machine learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction and outlook; the body was not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper linking quantum contextuality to inductive bias and expressivity of learning models, with a toy zero-sum-game problem.

assertions.value: The authors state that contextuality is tied to expressivity: contextual model classes that encode the inductive bias are generally more expressive than their noncontextual counterparts.
quotes: A consequence of this connection is that contextuality is tied to expressivity
contextual model classes that encode the inductive bias are generally more expressive than their noncontextual counterparts
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract statement; the proof was not checked in this partial read.

assertions.value: The authors state that, on an explicit toy problem based on learning the payoff behaviour of a zero-sum game, quantum learning models with the associated inductive bias outperform their corresponding classical surrogate models.
quotes: we construct an explicit toy learning problem
show through our toy problem that they outperform their corresponding classical surrogate models
assertions.certainty_reason: Result on a constructed toy problem in one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The advantage is shown against classical surrogate models on a constructed problem, not on real data.

assertions.value: The authors state that a pertinent open question for this work is whether the linearly conserved quantities they consider can be usefully encoded in classical models using a tractable amount of resources.
quotes: Perhaps the most pertinent question regarding this particular work is whether the linearly conserved quantities we consider
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own statement of an open limit of the result, Outlook, p.31.

papers.title_in_file: Simulating time evolution on distributed quantum computers
papers.what_it_is: A sparse Trotter-Suzuki decomposition for Hamiltonian simulation on distributed quantum computers with slow interconnects.

assertions.value: The authors state that fast local operations on monolithic devices can be leveraged to obtain an overall improved result fidelity even on distributed quantum computers where use of interconnects is costly.
quotes: we show that fast local operations on monolithic devices can be leveraged to obtain an overall improved result fidelity even on distributed quantum computers where the use of interconnects is costly.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical simulation result of one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that the overall quality of the approximation depends smoothly on the local sparsity and that the proliferation of local errors is slow.
quotes: We find that the overall quality of the approximation depends smoothly on the local sparsity and that the proliferation of local errors is slow.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical simulation result of one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that they simulate the non-equilibrium dynamics of transverse-field Ising and XY spin chain models.
quotes: We simulate non-equilibrium dynamics of transverse-field Ising and XY spin chain models
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of which models it tests, Abstract, p.1.
assertions.reader_inference: Results are shown for these two model families only.

papers.what_it_is: An analysis of maximum-likelihood quantum amplitude estimation (MLQAE), including exceptional amplitude values where it fails, and a heuristic fix.

assertions.value: The authors state that they deepen the analysis of MLQAE to put the algorithm in a more prescriptive form, including scenarios where quantum circuit depth is limited.
quotes: we deepen the analysis of MLQAE to put the algorithm in a more prescriptive form, including scenarios where quantum circuit depth is limited
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its scope, Abstract, p.1.

assertions.value: The authors state that they observe and explain particular ranges of exceptional values of the target amplitude for which the algorithm fails to achieve the desired precision.
quotes: for which the algorithm
fails to achieve the desired precision
assertions.certainty_reason: Analysis plus numerical observation in one study; the proof status was not checked in this partial read.

assertions.value: The authors state that they propose and numerically validate a heuristic modification to the algorithm to overcome the problem of exceptional values.
quotes: We then propose and numerically validate
a heuristic modification to the algorithm to overcome this problem
assertions.certainty_reason: Heuristic validated numerically in one study.

papers.title_in_file: Application of Quantum Machine Learning in a Higgs Physics Study at the CEPC
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, hardware results and discussion.
papers.what_it_is: A quantum kernel SVM applied to e+e- to ZH signal-versus-background classification, on simulators and on IBM and Origin Quantum hardware.

assertions.value: The authors report that, using 6 qubits on quantum computer simulators, they optimised the QSVM-Kernel algorithm and obtained a classification performance similar to the classical support-vector machine algorithm.
quotes: Using 6 qubits on quantum computer simulators, we optimised the QSVMKernel algorithm and obtained a classification performance similar to the classical support-vector machine algorithm.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result of one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The result is parity with the classical SVM, not an advantage.

assertions.value: The authors report ROC curve AUC values of 0.827 for the quantum simulator, 0.820 for Origin hardware and 0.789 for IBM hardware on the same analysis dataset.
quotes: Quantum Simulator (AUC = 0.827)
Origin Hardware (AUC = 0.820)
IBM Hardware (AUC = 0.789)
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result of one study on a small hardware dataset.

assertions.value: The authors state that the QSVM-Kernel algorithm scales quadratically with the size of the dataset, which they call not ideal.
quotes: the QSVMKernel algorithm scales quadratically with the size of the dataset
This is not ideal but can be mitigated by the better computational speed of future quantum computer hardware.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own statement of the algorithm's scaling limit, Discussion.
